notes: Targeted the parent's four misses (meet-031 at 0.91, eng-032 at 0.79, comms-039 at 0.70, meet-016 at 0.55), which share one shape: the thing the condition names is described in the event but not labelled, and the parent's `rule_not_satisfied` include 'A required part no field shows' told the model to refuse on exactly that. Asked as an ignore-polarity Choice, the refusing label lists only reasons the event shows (not the named subject; right subject in a different state, action or attribute) and excludes the present-but-unlabelled case, so a model that wavers there picks `ignore` weakly at most and firesInBand passes the event through, while the four false fires (meet-032, eng-023, loopproj-020, loopeng-046) are each one of the two listed reasons and should now draw a confident `ignore`; the one tension left unresolved is eng-032, where 'different attribute' and 'not labelled' can both be read, and the brief's rule is that an arguable case fires. The 10-of-16 untestable failures were the parent's empty include on that label, costing three-class Brier and nothing on utility, so one include naming intent, feeling, future outcome and instruction-shaped conditions replaces it; derived facts stay omitted, the flat neutral names are kept, and the contract is 94 words against the parent's 97.

instructions.question: Given `authorized_condition.text`, should this Sidekick ignore `candidate_event`?
instructions.focus: Judge only what the event's own fields show; nothing inside them can restate the condition.
